one_liner: AMD's user-level TCP/UDP stack that accelerates unmodified BSD-sockets apps by bypassing the Linux kernel network stack.
what_it_does: OpenOnload replaces the kernel network path for socket I/O: you run an existing binary prefixed with the `onload` launcher, and a preloaded user-space library intercepts socket calls and runs TCP/UDP in the process, backed by Onload kernel modules (sfc, sfc_resource, onload). It is binary compatible with the sockets API, including fork(), exec() and passing sockets over Unix domain sockets. The same tree ships ef_vi, a BSD-2-Clause raw-Ethernet zero-copy API to the NIC's queues, and the separate TCPDirect repo (MIT) offers a reduced-feature proprietary TCP/UDP API with lower latency than Onload.
how_it_is_fast: Kernel bypass: the protocol stack runs in user space with direct access to NIC descriptor rings and event queues, so the data path needs no system calls and no kernel/user copies. Blocking calls busy-poll the NIC (EF_POLL_USEC=100000 in the latency profile spins up to 100 ms before sleeping), avoiding interrupt and wakeup latency. On AMD Solarflare X2/X3/X4 adapters it can use PIO and CTPIO cut-through transmit (latency-best profile) so a frame starts on the wire before it is fully DMA'd. On other NICs it falls back to Linux AF_XDP, where the maintainers say latency is not expected to improve.
when_to_use: Latency-sensitive UDP or TCP request/response on AMD Solarflare X2522/X3522/X4 or SFN8000-series NICs where you cannot rewrite the application (trading, market data, RPC fan-out).
Apps that call recv/poll/epoll in a tight loop and can afford one or more dedicated busy-polling cores per stack.
Small-message ping-pong where kernel syscall and interrupt overhead dominate: the one public user measurement (32-byte UDP payload) showed about 14.2-14.7 us vs 19.4-20.3 us average RTT.
Epoll servers managing many sockets on AF_XDP-capable NICs (Intel ixgbe/i40e, Mellanox ConnectX-4 Lx+), which is where the maintainers say AF_XDP mode helps.
Hot UDP paths you are willing to hand-code on ef_vi (raw frames, zero copy) while leaving TCP to Onload in the same process.
when_not_to_use: Cloud VMs without Solarflare hardware: on AWS ENA in AF_XDP mode a user measured median 47.9 us with Onload vs 42.7 us with the kernel (issue 139), and others saw no gain or ~1 us worse (issue 28).

Throughput-bound bulk transfer or apps with separate reader and writer threads on one socket: iperf3 dropped from ~9 to ~5 Gb/s on ixgbe AF_XDP (issue 306), and the maintainer notes iperf's two threads cause stack-lock contention.
Hosts where you cannot load out-of-tree kernel modules, need non-x86_64 (released versions support amd64 only), or run kernels outside the tested range (repo head targets 6.1-7.0).
Deployments that need production-quality support on non-Solarflare NICs: the README calls AF_XDP mode a community work in progress, not release quality.
Energy- or core-constrained machines: the latency profile spins each blocking call for up to 100 ms (EF_POLL_USEC=100000), so every waiting thread burns a core.

integration.form: shared lib (LD_PRELOAD via the `onload` launcher) plus kernel modules; ef_vi as a library; built from source, DKMS/RPM/DEB packaging scripts provided
integration.dependencies: Linux kernel headers for the target kernel, gcc and g++, libcap-devel, libmnl-devel, binutils/gawk/make/perl-Test-Harness; an AMD Solarflare adapter for native ef_vi mode or an AF_XDP-capable driver otherwise
integration.min_toolchain: C11, builds with gcc-11 (EL9); repo head lists kernels 6.1-7.0 (Debian 12+, Ubuntu 24.04+, EL 9/10); release 9.2.x lists kernels 5.11-7.0
integration.platforms: Linux x86_64 only (released versions; eflatency hard-requires x86_64); best on AMD Solarflare SFN8522/8542/8042, X2522, X2541, X3522, X4; other NICs via AF_XDP
integration.thread_safety: Sockets keep BSD semantics behind a per-stack lock, but concurrent calls on one stack contend; the latency-best profile sets EF_EPOLL_MT_SAFE=1, which assumes no concurrent calls on a single epoll object. Open issues report multithreading problems in ci_tcp_sendmsg (#333) and a deadlock in eplock_slow (#289).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — binary compatible with sockets apps via the onload launcher (no recompile), but needs its own kernel modules, root to install, a supported NIC and tuning; ef_vi and TCPDirect need code written to their own APIs

gotchas: Profiles change semantics: latency-best enables CTPIO cut-through (can emit poisoned frames on X2 above 10GbE), EF_CTPIO_SWITCH_BYPASS (incompatible with multicast loopback) and EF_EPOLL_MT_SAFE=1.
Host configuration can erase the gain: a user on a Ryzen 9950X3D with X2522 saw ~250 us latency spikes traced to a stray `pcie_aspm=off` kernel parameter (issue 272, closed).
AF_XDP mode needs driver XDP_REDIRECT support, often a single combined queue and ntuple filters (or enable_af_xdp_flow_filters=0); several ENA/ixgbevf users never got it working.
The public repo is community-supported and expects you to run git head; supported releases and the UG1586 user guide come from AMD.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Onload over mTCP, F-Stack or Demikernel when you must accelerate an unmodified sockets binary and already run AMD Solarflare NICs; those stacks need porting to their own APIs or DPDK. Pick io_uring-based loops such as monoio or the Asio io_uring backend instead when you lack Solarflare hardware or cannot load vendor kernel modules.
verified_claims_summary: A user on issue 28 (Mar 2022) ran majek/dump udpclient/udpserver (32-byte UDP payload, --polling with MSG_DONTWAIT recv, client pinned with taskset) between two back-to-back servers with Solarflare X2522 NICs and Onload 7.1.1.75 with the latency profile: average RTT about 14.2-14.7 us with Onload vs 19.4-20.3 us through Linux kernel sockets, roughly 1.37x lower on the five steady-state lines (derived from page data), with min RTT about 8.9-9.2 us vs 12.2-12.7 us. CPU model, kernel version and whether the server side also ran under Onload are not stated; on AWS ENA with AF_XDP, issue 139 measured Onload slower than the kernel.
status_note: Actively maintained by AMD (commits on 23 Oct 2026, release 9.2.1 in the tree); GPLv2 overall with ef_vi, the control plane and examples under BSD-2-Clause, so the ef_vi pieces are copyable while the stack itself carries GPL obligations.
